items.text: Bavaria's Health Protection Act (Gesundheitsschutzgesetz, art. 3) bans smoking, heating or vaping cannabis wherever tobacco smoking is banned indoors, and also in the outdoor areas of restaurants and bars, including beer gardens, and across Volksfest grounds such as the Oktoberfest (rides, stalls, walkways and tents). Councils can add bans by ordinance for set crowded public places (art. 8). The fine is up to EUR 1,500 (about A$2,384), and up to EUR 5,000 (A$7,945) for a repeat (art. 10). AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293.

Bavaria's fines catalogue for the federal Cannabis Act (in force 1 April 2024) sets standard fines for a first deliberate offence: EUR 1,000 for using cannabis in the presence of minors (about A$1,589); EUR 500 for using it within 100 m of the entrance to schools, playgrounds, child and youth facilities or public sports grounds (A$795); EUR 300 in pedestrian zones between 7 am and 8 pm (A$477); and EUR 500 to EUR 1,000 for carrying more than 25 g, up to 30 g, away from home (A$795 to A$1,589). Fines double for a repeat of the same kind within three years and are halved for negligence. AUD at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293.

On 24 November 2025 the Bavarian Administrative Court ruled that the state palace and gardens administration's ban on cannabis use in Munich's English Garden, Hofgarten and Finanzgarten is invalid (case 10 N 25.826), so the federal Cannabis Act rules apply there again. Beer gardens there remain under the Health Protection Act ban on outdoor dining areas.
